title: Position-conditioned word and stroke drawers
method:
A copyist has drawers of word cards and a smaller table of strokes. Separate the left edge, right edge, single-word lines, and interior, then split the interior into three equal intervals of relative position. Count complete forms in public ZL practice-training text, excluding marked forms. A drawer specializes from whole book to edge, line kind, zone, Currier dialect, section, and preceding word's final EVA-basic glyph. At each nonempty level prefer its counts with probability N/(N+2V), where N is the number of cards and V the number of forms in the drawer; otherwise retain the less specific level. Draw in proportion to the chosen counts. Public training supplies line lengths by line kind, dialect, and section with the same backoff. For each line the book layout supplies only page order, line kind, paragraph opening, dialect, and section. At interior slots, four of 32 rolls take a card from the current or last two lines on this page, chosen uniformly across written slots. Four rolls build a new form from a second-order stroke drawer specialized by line kind, zone and dialect, with START and STOP entries and a fourteen-stroke limit; a start table can use the preceding word's last stroke. The remainder take a stored word. Edges take a stored word. An ambiguous stroke segmentation or any four-word run found in the manuscript is rejected and redrawn. Full transliteration wording is used solely for this stock copy guard. Layout uses cut book. Seed 408 was chosen before scoring and emits 5,225 lines and 38,946 tokens. Matched controls pool the three interior zones, keeping the same layout, edge classes, and mixture rolls. Seed 409 is a sensitivity comparison. The procedure has no rules that name any tested pattern. Training counts in the drawers already encode positional observations, so the comparison tests compatibility with a context-dependent copying process and cannot identify a historical writer's procedure.

Public practice: the fixed specimen reproduced the matched t-versus-k position effect (F-030, +0.050981 of the line, 399-draw page-bootstrap interval +0.019248 to +0.077382, 764 k / 499 t / 31 pages). Its matched ch-versus-sh effect did not clear zero (F-029, +0.005167; interval -0.029274 to +0.044028). Seed 409 switched the two individual outcomes. Neither pooled control cleared zero for either effect. The fitted generator retained next-glyph predictability (F-013, 1.966170 bits on the primary run) but did not reach the singleton-type threshold (F-014, 0.603732 versus 0.667). The primary seed is kept as planned. These are practice numbers.
